summary: The orchestration component runs multi-agent loops. Its WorkflowExecutor (src/orchestration/workflows.rs) drives a DAG of WorkflowSteps (Tool, Shell, Llm, Condition, Loop, SubWorkflow, Guardrail) with retries, timeouts, and cycle detection; its Swarm coordinator drives role-typed Agents through task assignment, weighted Votes, and Decisions resolved by a ConflictStrategy over SharedMemory; MultiAgentChat fans one completion out per Agent under a BudgetGuard and a tokio Semaphore; and the VisualFeedbackLoop iterates act-capture-evaluate against a VisualScore quality_threshold. On the loop it is the control driver that spawns, sequences, and reconciles parallel sub-loops.
context_basis: Recommendations were formed with src/orchestration/ read in the context of the full engine under a ~600k budget framing; fan-out and swarm coordination assume a shared budget that must be guarded across many concurrent sub-agents.

examples.title: Execute a Workflow as a dependency-ordered DAG
examples.intent: Run steps in dependency order so each starts only when its inputs are ready.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: WorkflowExecutor::execute loads a Workflow, builds a WorkflowContext, and runs WorkflowSteps respecting depends_on, so the control layer sequences the sub-loop deterministically.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing edges between step nodes declares depends_on links; the executor runs them in the drawn order.
touch_interaction.visual: Step nodes wire up with directed arrows; each lights green as its StepStatus hits Completed, the next arming only when its parents are done.

examples.mini_scenario: The user wires clone before test before review; WorkflowExecutor::execute runs each only after its predecessor's StepResult reads Completed.
examples.pitfall: depends_on must form a DAG; a dependency cycle stalls the workflow, which is why WorkflowContext tracks an executing_steps stack for cycle detection.

examples.title: Retry a failing step with backoff and a timeout
examples.intent: Give a flaky step bounded retries without letting it hang the loop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: WorkflowExecutor::execute_step_with_retry wraps a step in a tokio::select against its RetryConfig timeout and retries up to max_attempts with delay, so the control layer contains transient failures.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a step opens its RetryConfig dial; each attempt animates a countdown against the timeout ring.
touch_interaction.visual: A retry counter ticks and a timeout ring drains; on timeout the ring snaps red and the step marks Failed.

examples.mini_scenario: A network tool step fails once, waits the backoff, succeeds on retry two, and returns a Completed StepResult.
examples.pitfall: The timeout must actually cancel the step future; a retry loop without cancellation lets a hung step run past its timeout budget.

examples.title: Branch the loop with a Condition step
examples.intent: Choose the next steps based on a runtime condition over the context.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A Condition StepType evaluates its 'if' via WorkflowContext::evaluate_condition (success(), failed(), equality) and runs the then or else branch inline, so the reason stage forks the workflow path at runtime.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a condition node reveals its two branch arms; the arm whose predicate holds lights up.
touch_interaction.visual: A diamond node shows then/else arms; the true arm glows green and the false arm dims when evaluate_condition resolves.

examples.mini_scenario: If tests succeed the condition lights the review branch; if they failed it lights the notify branch instead.
examples.pitfall: Branch steps are marked control-flow-managed so the top-level pass does not run them twice; forgetting that double-executes both arms.

examples.title: Iterate a Loop step over a list
examples.intent: Run a body of steps once per item, keyed per iteration.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A Loop StepType splits its 'in' list and runs 'do' steps per item, storing each result as step_id@idx in the WorkflowContext, so the control layer expands one node into an indexed sequence.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading a loop node unrolls it into one body-instance per item laid out in a row.
touch_interaction.visual: The loop node fans into indexed instances; each runs and greens in turn, the aggregate node summing their states.

examples.mini_scenario: A loop over three services runs the deploy body for each; results store as deploy@0, deploy@1, deploy@2.
examples.pitfall: Dependency lookup is iteration-aware (dep@idx first, then plain dep); resolving a dep without the index reads the wrong iteration's result.

examples.title: Substitute variables shell-safely into a Shell step
examples.intent: Inject context values into a shell command without opening an injection hole.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: WorkflowContext::substitute_shell_safe POSIX-quotes interpolated values before a Shell StepType runs, so the foundation layer prevents a malicious variable from escaping the command.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a shell node highlights each interpolated token wrapped in a quote shield.
touch_interaction.visual: Variable tokens in the command render inside a shield capsule; an unsafe raw value flashes a warning before quoting.

examples.mini_scenario: A step runs 'git clone ${repo_url}'; the URL is POSIX-quoted so a value with a semicolon cannot append a second command.
examples.pitfall: Plain WorkflowContext::substitute must never feed a Shell step; using it instead of substitute_shell_safe reintroduces command injection.

examples.title: Enforce a Guardrail step that fails closed
examples.intent: Block the workflow when a safety condition is violated.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A Guardrail StepType evaluates its condition via the GuardrailEngine over a GuardrailContext; a block or unknown EvaluationResult returns an error, so the verify stage halts the loop rather than proceeding unsafely.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a guardrail node runs its check; a violation slams a barrier across the outgoing edge.
touch_interaction.visual: A gate node lowers a red barrier on block, an amber caution on warn, and stays open green on pass.

examples.mini_scenario: A guardrail checks the diff stays in scope; a violation returns Err with block severity and the workflow stops.
examples.pitfall: Unknown must fail closed like block; treating an unresolved guardrail as allow lets an unevaluated safety check pass silently.

examples.title: Nest a SubWorkflow with cycle detection
examples.intent: Compose a workflow out of reusable sub-workflows without infinite recursion.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A SubWorkflow StepType executes with an appended WorkflowContext::workflow_call_stack and a recursion_depth cap, so the control layer nests sub-loops while detecting call cycles across workflow boundaries.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a sub-workflow node dives into its inner canvas; a breadcrumb tracks the workflow_call_stack.
touch_interaction.visual: The node opens into a nested canvas; the breadcrumb trail grows, flashing red if a name repeats in the stack.

examples.mini_scenario: A release workflow calls the build sub-workflow, whose outputs merge back; a self-call would trip the cycle guard.
examples.pitfall: The call stack must track names across boundaries; depth counting alone misses a cycle between two mutually-calling workflows.

examples.title: Assign a SwarmTask to the highest-trust idle Agent
examples.intent: Route each task to an available specialist most likely to do it well.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Swarm::assign_task matches a SwarmTask's required_roles to idle Agents by highest trust_score and sets them Working, so the act stage dispatches work to the fittest agent per role.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a task tile onto the swarm auto-snaps it to the idle agent of the required role with the best trust_score.
touch_interaction.visual: The task tile flies to the chosen agent node, which lights Working; passed-over agents dim briefly.

examples.mini_scenario: An architecture task requiring Architect and Security roles snaps to the two idle specialists with the highest trust scores.
examples.pitfall: Only idle agents are eligible; assigning to a Working agent creates a zombie task, so completion must return agents to Idle.

examples.title: Recycle Agents back to Idle on task completion
examples.intent: Return finished agents to the pool so future tasks can use them.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Swarm::complete_task records the result, updates the Agent's trust_score and task counts, then sets it Idle, so the control layer keeps the agent pool circulating instead of freezing agents in Completed.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a Working agent that just finished sends it back to the idle pool with an updated trust badge.
touch_interaction.visual: The agent node flips from Working amber to Idle green; its trust badge ticks up on success or down on failure.

examples.mini_scenario: A Coder finishes its task; complete_task bumps its trust_score, marks the task Completed, and returns it Idle for the next assignment.
examples.pitfall: Forgetting to set the agent Idle after completion leaves it stuck Completed forever, starving the pool of that AgentRole.

examples.title: Open a Decision and collect weighted Votes
examples.intent: Let the swarm decide among options with each vote weighted by expertise and trust.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Swarm::create_decision opens a Decision; each Agent's Vote carries weighted_value = confidence x role_priority x trust_score, so the reason stage aggregates opinions by earned authority.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping each agent casts its vote onto the decision node; vote bars grow by their weighted_value.
touch_interaction.visual: Option bars fill as votes land, each segment sized by the voter's weight; the leading option pulses ahead.

examples.mini_scenario: On an architecture choice, the Security agent's high-priority high-trust vote outweighs two low-confidence votes for the alternative.
examples.pitfall: weighted_value is confidence times priority times trust; dropping any factor lets a confident but untrusted agent sway the decision unfairly.

examples.title: Resolve a conflicted Decision by ConflictStrategy
examples.intent: Break a tie or clash of votes with an explicit resolution rule.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Swarm::resolve_conflict applies a ConflictStrategy (PriorityWins, ConfidenceWins, MajorityWins, HumanIntervention, AcceptAll), so the verify stage turns a Conflict Decision into a determinate outcome or escalates it.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the strategy dial on a conflicted decision recomputes the winner under each ConflictStrategy rule.
touch_interaction.visual: The dial cycles strategy labels; the winning option re-highlights per rule, HumanIntervention greys all and raises a hand icon.

examples.mini_scenario: A split vote is resolved by PriorityWins, letting the Security agent's option win; switching to HumanIntervention would escalate instead.
examples.pitfall: HumanIntervention returns no automatic outcome; treating its None as a default choice silently picks for the human it meant to consult.

examples.title: Coordinate agents through bounded SharedMemory
examples.intent: Let agents exchange intermediate results without direct coupling.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SharedMemory offers write/read/peek/delete with an access log bounded to a ring buffer, so the foundation layer gives the swarm a common blackboard that cannot grow unbounded.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing from an agent to the memory slab writes a keyed MemoryEntry; drawing from the slab to another agent reads it.
touch_interaction.visual: A memory slab shows keyed cells; writes drop glowing cells, reads pull threads out, the access log scrolling beneath.

examples.mini_scenario: The Architect writes a design key to SharedMemory; the Coder reads it and its access_count increments in the log.
examples.pitfall: The access log is a bounded ring buffer; relying on it for a full audit trail loses the oldest MemoryAccess records once it rolls over.

examples.title: Fan one completion out per Agent under a semaphore
examples.intent: Run many specialist perspectives in parallel with bounded concurrency.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MultiAgentChat::run_task spawns one chat_completion per Agent gated by a tokio Semaphore sized to MultiAgentConfig::max_concurrency, so the act stage parallelizes perspectives without unbounded fan-out.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the task node forks one lane per agent; only max_concurrency lanes run at once, the rest queue for a permit.
touch_interaction.visual: Agent lanes light up in parallel up to the concurrency cap; queued lanes wait greyed until a permit frees.

examples.mini_scenario: One prompt fans out to Reviewer, Tester, and Security agents; with concurrency 2, Security waits until a semaphore permit frees.
examples.pitfall: The semaphore bounds concurrency, not total spend; without the BudgetGuard the parallel fan-out can still blow the token budget.

examples.title: Guard the fan-out spend with a BudgetGuard
examples.intent: Cap total tokens and cost across all parallel agents.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MultiAgentChat wraps the fan-out in a BudgetGuard enforcing max_budget_tokens and max_cost_usd, so the control layer skips agents once the shared budget is exhausted.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the budget bar shows it draining as each agent reserves its estimate; agents past the line grey out.
touch_interaction.visual: A shared budget bar depletes with each launch; when it hits zero, remaining agent lanes stamp 'skipped: budget'.

examples.mini_scenario: Four agents fan out but the budget covers three; the fourth is pessimistically skipped and emits AgentFailed instead of overspending.
examples.pitfall: Estimate pessimistically before launch; a naive optimistic estimate can admit an agent that then overshoots the shared cap.

examples.title: Cancel remaining agents on first failure (FailFast)
examples.intent: Stop wasting budget on siblings once one agent has failed the task.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Under MultiAgentFailurePolicy::FailFast, the first agent error signals a shared tokio::sync::Notify that cancels the remaining tasks, so the control layer aborts the fan-out early.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A failing lane flicks a cancel wave across the sibling lanes, halting them mid-run.
touch_interaction.visual: The failed lane flashes red and a cancellation ripple sweeps the row; sibling lanes freeze and grey out.

examples.mini_scenario: With FailFast set, the Tester agent errors; the Notify fires and the still-running Reviewer and Security lanes cancel.
examples.pitfall: FailFast trades completeness for cost; choosing it when partial results matter throws away work BestEffort would have kept.

examples.title: Stream MultiAgentEvents as agents progress
examples.intent: Observe the fan-out live rather than waiting for the final batch.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MultiAgentChat emits MultiAgentEvents (AgentStarted, AgentCompleted, AgentFailed, AllCompleted) over an mpsc channel, so the perceive stage watches the parallel loop unfold in real time.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the event stream node opens a live feed of agent lifecycle events scrolling as they fire.
touch_interaction.visual: An event ticker scrolls: green Started/Completed rows, red Failed rows, a final AllCompleted banner summing durations.

examples.mini_scenario: The user taps the stream and watches AgentStarted then AgentCompleted rows arrive per agent, ending in AllCompleted.
examples.pitfall: Events use non-blocking try_send; if the channel fills, events drop, so the stream is a view, not a guaranteed-complete log.

examples.title: Iterate a VisualFeedbackLoop to a quality threshold
examples.intent: Refine a visual output until a critic scores it good enough.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VisualFeedbackLoop runs act-capture-evaluate until VisualScore.overall meets quality_threshold or max_iterations, so the verify stage closes a self-correcting visual sub-loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the visual loop unrolls its iterations; each shows a capture thumbnail and its score climbing toward the line.
touch_interaction.visual: A row of iteration thumbnails rises in score; the loop stops and glows green when a thumbnail crosses the threshold line.

examples.mini_scenario: A UI render scores 72 then 81; the second iteration crosses the 0.8 quality_threshold and the loop returns a VisualLoopResult with threshold_met true.
examples.pitfall: max_iterations must cap the loop; a strict threshold the critic never reaches spins forever without the iteration ceiling.

examples.title: Parse a critic response into a dimensioned VisualScore
examples.intent: Turn a vision model's prose into per-dimension scores plus suggestions.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: parse_critic_response tolerates markdown fences and extracts a VisualScore (composition, hierarchy, readability, consistency, accessibility, weighted overall via compute_overall), so the reason stage gets actionable per-axis feedback.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a critique node breaks it into five dimension gauges plus a suggestions list.
touch_interaction.visual: Five radial gauges (composition, hierarchy, readability, consistency, accessibility) fill; a suggestions panel lists fixes below.

examples.mini_scenario: The critic returns markdown-fenced JSON; parse_critic_response extracts accessibility 62 and the suggestion 'add focus indicators'.
examples.pitfall: Overall is a weighted average of the axes (compute_overall weights readability 0.25); recomputing it with equal weights misreports quality the loop then chases wrongly.

examples.title: Shed load when the Swarm hits resource pressure
examples.intent: Refuse new tasks when the swarm is already saturated.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Swarm::queue_task checks crate::resource::ResourcePressure and fails to enqueue when it is High or Critical, so the control layer applies backpressure instead of overcommitting agents.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the queue shows a pressure gauge; at Critical the intake slot slams shut and rejects the drop.
touch_interaction.visual: A pressure gauge rides green to red; at High/Critical the queue intake flashes closed and bounces the incoming task tile.

examples.mini_scenario: Under Critical pressure the user tries to queue a task; queue_task rejects it so the overloaded swarm is not pushed further.
examples.pitfall: Backpressure must reject at intake, not mid-run; admitting a task under Critical pressure just moves the overload downstream.

examples.title: Sweep timed-out Decisions to keep the swarm live
examples.intent: Prevent pending decisions from blocking the swarm indefinitely.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Swarm::sweep_timed_out_decisions marks Decisions older than decision_timeout_secs (default 300, set via with_decision_timeout) as TimedOut, so the control layer unblocks agents waiting on a vote that never resolved.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking across the decision board sweeps stale pending decisions, stamping the overdue ones TimedOut.
touch_interaction.visual: Pending decision cards past their age flash and stamp a grey 'TimedOut' seal; agents waiting on them release.

examples.mini_scenario: A decision sits unresolved past its 300s timeout; the sweep marks it TimedOut so the agents holding for its outcome move on.
examples.pitfall: A TimedOut decision has no consensus outcome; downstream logic must handle the timeout branch rather than assume a resolved choice.
